items.context: The sidebar needs to track active tab, search query, filter selections, and sort preferences. This state is used by multiple sub-components (search bar, tab bar, filter bar, content lists). Options range from a single local reducer in Sidebar.tsx to a dedicated Zustand store.

options.label: Single useReducer in Sidebar.tsx
options.rationale: All sidebar state is local to one component subtree — no other surface needs it. Follows react-coherence 'local state first' principle. URL sync happens at this level via useSearchParams. Simplest approach, no new store files.

options.label: Dedicated Zustand sidebar-ui store
options.rationale: Allows other components (e.g., graph canvas, keyboard shortcuts) to read/write sidebar state. More infrastructure but enables future features like 'jump to tab from graph context menu'.

items.context: Each tab (Activity, Backlog, Captures, Initiatives, Executions) needs its own rendering logic with entity-specific metadata display. The question is how to organize these — as separate files or inline within the sidebar.

options.label: Separate file per tab component
options.rationale: Each tab in its own file (e.g., BacklogTab.tsx, CapturesTab.tsx) under surfaces/graph/components/sidebar/. Clean separation, easy to test individually, follows existing pattern of component-per-file. Sidebar.tsx becomes a thin orchestrator.

options.label: All tabs inline in Sidebar.tsx
options.rationale: Keeps everything in one file. Simpler for a small number of tabs, but Sidebar.tsx would grow to 400+ lines. Harder to navigate.

items.context: The Initiatives and Executions tabs need data sources. The backlog store and capture store exist, but I need to verify whether initiative and execution data is already available in stores or only fetched on-demand. If stores don't exist, we need to decide whether to create them or fetch inline.

options.label: Use existing stores/services — create thin wrappers only if missing
options.rationale: The graph-data-store likely already has initiative and execution data since the graph renders these as nodes. Tap into existing data flow rather than creating parallel fetch paths. Only create a new store if the data truly isn't available anywhere.

options.label: Create dedicated initiative-store and execution-store
options.rationale: Follows the pattern of backlog-store and capture-store. Ensures sidebar has its own data lifecycle independent of graph rendering. More work upfront but cleaner separation.

items.freeform: Whatever you think is the best, most professional long-term solution

items.topic: URL param encoding strategy for filters
items.context: Filters and sort state need URL persistence for shareability and back-button support. With multiple filter dimensions (status, priority, kind, tags) plus sort field and direction, the URL could become long.

options.label: Individual params with compact keys
options.rationale: E.g., ?st=backlog,ready&pr=1-3&sort=priority&dir=asc. Human-readable, easy to debug, standard URLSearchParams usage. Only non-default values are serialized. Matches existing pattern (GraphWorkspace already uses ?select=nodeId).

options.label: Single encoded JSON param
options.rationale: E.g., ?sidebar=eyJ0YWIi... (base64 JSON). Compact but opaque, hard to debug, and breaks if the encoding changes.

items.text: The existing SearchBar component (components/ui/search-bar.tsx) wraps the Input component with a Search icon and accepts value/onChange/placeholder props. It can be reused directly — no need to build a new search input. The searchDebounceMs config (default 300ms) is available via useRuntimeConfig.
